B. Is this measure already running in Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Travel and accommodation support for patients far from the university hospital. Patients who must travel for surgery or weeks of radiotherapy get a booked patient hotel, organised transport and a named contact, so that distance is not the reason to choose a non-curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: The only evidence is an association from England: patients with the longest travel time had 0.60 times the odds of surgery; no study measured the effect of travel support itself.
supported_en: Crawford 2009 (British Journal of Cancer) reports that patients in northern England with the longest travel time had 0.60 times the odds of lung cancer surgery of the nearest.
not_supported_en: No page shows that travel or lodging support raises the curative-intent share, or by how much (the model assumes 1 percentage point).
in_use_quote: Jos tulet pitkän matkan takaa eikä vointisi ole sellainen, että sinun tarvitsisi jäädä sairaalan vuodeosastolle, sinä ja läheisesi voitte majoittua sairaalan lähellä sijaitsevassa potilaskodissa.
in_use_summary_en: OYS in Oulu runs a 63-bed patient home for patients who come from far away; patients book it themselves, and Kela pays back part of the cost.
missing_en: No page shows organised transport or a named contact who books lodging for patients from Central Ostrobothnia; at OYS the patient books the room.
summary_en: OYS runs a patient home with 63 beds (32 + 31), 400–700 m from the hospital, for patients who come from far away, at 41.98 euros per night for an adult, part of which Kela reimburses. OYS's lung cancer pathway page says the university hospital gives lung cancer surgery and radiotherapy, so Soite patients have to travel to Oulu. The only effect evidence is an association, not a test of travel support: in northern England (Crawford 2009, British Journal of Cancer), patients with the longest travel time had 0.60 times the odds of surgery of the nearest.
unanswered_en: No search was made for transport arrangements from Kokkola to Oulu or for a support coordinator for cancer patients at Soite, and no study testing travel support was found.
